headline: Highest risk is prompt-injection/data-flow confusion from Firecrawl’s web-content ingestion into Whisper’s audio-only pipeline; other risks are mostly low or none.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Firecrawl ingests web content and exposes MCP-compatible/API outputs, while Whisper is audio-only with no file or network ingestion path. A direct injection bridge is not documented, so the main pathway would require unusual manual transfer of Firecrawl text into a downstream parser. That makes the blast radius small and the interaction indirect.
conditions: IF Firecrawl output is manually copied into a prompt or parser that Whisper consumes, injection risk appears.
IF an orchestrator adds a shared text channel between the agents, the severity increases.
mitigations: Keep Firecrawl outputs out of any instruction-following prompt.
Use a fixed schema or delimiter when passing text between agents.
Disable manual copy-paste handoffs for untrusted web content.
Add a short provenance label to every Firecrawl-derived artifact.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Firecrawl touches API keys and web content, but Whisper has no filesystem read, no network egress, and no API calls, so there is no documented path for Whisper to exfiltrate Firecrawl data. The pair can still leak if an operator manually moves sensitive Firecrawl artifacts into Whisper inputs, but that is an unusual configuration with limited blast radius.
conditions: IF Firecrawl artifacts containing API keys are manually supplied to Whisper, those contents may be exposed in transcripts or logs.
IF a wrapper adds shared storage readable by Whisper, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Do not pass secrets-bearing Firecrawl outputs into Whisper.
Redact API keys before any cross-agent transfer.
Store Firecrawl artifacts in a separate directory with restricted access.
Review wrapper logs for accidental inclusion of sensitive text.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Firecrawl can use APIs and multiple instances, but Whisper cannot write files, modify git state, or use MCP, and it has no network egress. With no overlapping write surface or shared mutable resource documented, a capability conflict between the pair is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same directory, conflict risk would no longer be none.
IF Whisper is wrapped with additional write tooling, reassess this verdict.
mitigations: Keep Whisper in read-only, no-write mode.
Avoid shared mutable workspaces between the agents.
Run Firecrawl jobs in isolated per-task directories.
Add orchestration-level locking if shared outputs are introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Firecrawl can produce scraped web content and structured data, but Whisper is a speech model with no action-taking authority and no documented downstream automation. The pair therefore lacks the high-risk pattern where one agent’s output directly drives irreversible actions; any cascade would require an extra orchestrator layer not shown here.
conditions: IF a third system treats Firecrawl output as authoritative and converts it into actions, cascading error risk rises.
IF Whisper is used to transcribe instructions that are then executed elsewhere, reassess.
mitigations: Require human review of Firecrawl-derived facts before action.
Mark Whisper transcripts as unverified input.
Separate extraction from execution steps.
Log source URLs alongside any derived claims.

E_compliance.rationale: Firecrawl handles web content, structured data, screenshots, and API keys, while Whisper only touches audio/speech. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented between them, so compliance risk is limited to operator-driven transfer of regulated data into Firecrawl. The other agent is not cited because no regulated-data handling is shown for Whisper.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is routed into Firecrawl, compliance review is required.
IF Whisper is used to process regulated audio and then forwarded to Firecrawl, reassess residency and retention.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to Firecrawl.
Redact identifiers before scraping or transcription.
Document retention for Firecrawl outputs.
Confirm any regulated workflow has a DPA and approved storage region.
